issues.legal_issue: A further renewal of a mining lease is invalid when the required reasons are not recorded or relevant considerations bearing on mineral development are not addressed.
material_facts: The leaseholder sought a second renewal of its lease.
The first government authorization granting the renewal did not state reasons for finding renewal to be in the interest of mineral development.
The later authorization gave reasons for reducing the area but did not consider the earlier committee report, the Supreme Court’s decision relying on that report, or the National Mineral Policy.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was justified in setting aside both renewal authorizations because they did not satisfy the requirements of Section 8(3).
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 8(3) of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957, as applicable to the application, a further renewal may be authorized only if the Central Government considers it necessary in the interests of mineral development and records reasons for doing so. The requirement is a safeguard against arbitrariness and must be followed strictly; the reasons must reflect proper consideration of relevant factors.

predicates.further_lease_renewal_proceeding: A government body considered whether to authorize a further renewal of an existing mining lease.
predicates.reasons_not_recorded: The government body authorized renewal without recording why it considered renewal necessary for mineral development.
predicates.relevant_mineral_development_factors_ign: The government body did not consider relevant policy or prior findings bearing on mineral development.

issues.definition: If a further lease renewal is being considered and reasons are absent or relevant mineral-development factors are ignored, the renewal authorization is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A government deciding a mineral lease application must explain a departure from a comprehensive report that has been recognized as relevant to lease decisions.
material_facts: A prior committee had comprehensively examined chromite mining and made findings and recommendations concerning leases and supply.
The Supreme Court had relied on that committee’s report and stated that it would assist governments in deciding lease applications and future policy.
The later government renewal decision did not refer to the report or explain a departure from it.
issues.conclusion: The Central Government was not bound to follow the report’s recommendations, but it was required to record reasons for departing from them; the High Court was justified in considering the report and the earlier decision.
issues.legal_principle: In Indian Metals & Ferro Alloys Ltd. v. Union of India, AIR 1991 SC 818, [1992] Supp. 1 SCC 91, the Court relied on the Rao Committee report and recognized its usefulness in decisions on chromite leases. A government is not bound to adopt the report’s recommendations, but must give reasons for departing from a relevant, comprehensive report, particularly when valuable, long-term leases are involved. Section 8(3) supplies the requirement to record reasons for further renewal.

predicates.mineral_lease_decision_proceeding: A government body considered whether to grant or renew a mineral lease.
predicates.comprehensive_relevant_report_exists: A prior committee produced a comprehensive report relevant to the mineral lease decision.
predicates.government_departed_without_reasons: The government body did not follow the report and did not record reasons for departing from it.

issues.definition: When a government body decides a mineral lease matter in the presence of a comprehensive relevant report, it must explain an unexplained departure from that report.

issues.legal_issue: Prospective applicants with a legitimate stake in the outcome of a lease renewal may be heard during consideration of the renewal.
material_facts: Other manufacturers had applied, or intended to apply, for mining leases over land included in the existing lease.
Renewing the entire lease could prevent the other applicants from obtaining any part of that land.
The High Court directed that the prospective applicants be heard, and the committee heard them during its reconsideration.
issues.conclusion: The High Court and the committee were justified in hearing prospective applicants because they could be affected by the renewal decision and had a legitimate stake in the proper formulation of the relevant policy.
issues.legal_principle: The Court accepted the High Court’s treatment of the prospective applicants as proper parties, even if they were not necessary parties. Those likely to be affected by a lease decision, and those with a legitimate stake in the formulation of an important policy, may be heard. Rules 59 and 60 of the Mineral Concession Rules did not prevent their participation in these proceedings.

predicates.lease_renewal_review_proceeding: A court or government body considered a challenge to, or reconsideration of, a mining lease renewal.
predicates.prospective_applicants_have_legitimate_s: Prospective applicants could be adversely affected by the renewal and had a legitimate interest in the decision.

issues.definition: In a lease renewal proceeding, prospective applicants with a legitimate stake in the outcome may be heard.

issues.legal_issue: The concept of mineral development in deciding mineral leases includes comparative assessment of captive mining needs and equitable distribution, with capacity to exploit the ore effectively as a predominant consideration.
material_facts: The lease area held a substantial share of the country’s chromite reserves, while other manufacturers had established industries and claimed inadequate access to raw material.
The committee assessed the captive requirements of the leaseholder and other manufacturers and considered their ability to use the ore.
The committee concluded that renewal of the entire area would exceed the leaseholder’s needs and could deprive other needy manufacturers of raw material.
issues.conclusion: The committee correctly treated captive mining requirements and equitable distribution as relevant to mineral development, assessed comparatively rather than as an automatic entitlement for every industry; the capacity to exploit the ore effectively is a predominant consideration.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered Sections 3(c), 6 and 8 of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, the Rao Committee report as treated in Indian Metals & Ferro Alloys Ltd. v. Union of India, AIR 1991 SC 818, [1992] Supp. 1 SCC 91, the National Mineral Policy, 1993, and the Orissa Industrial Policy, 1992. It also considered Articles 39(b) and 14 of the Constitution. The captive requirement of an industry is relevant on a comparative basis; it does not entitle every industry to a lease. The capacity of an industry to exploit the ore effectively is a predominant consideration, and equitable distribution among needy users may be considered.

rule.if: mineral_lease_allocation_proceeding and scarce_mineral_resource and competing_needy_industries and captive_use_needs_assessed

predicates.mineral_lease_allocation_proceeding: A government body considered the allocation or renewal of a lease for a mineral resource.
predicates.scarce_mineral_resource: The mineral resource available for allocation was limited in relation to demand.
predicates.competing_needy_industries: More than one established industry needed the mineral as raw material.
predicates.captive_use_needs_assessed: The decision-maker assessed how much mineral the industries needed for use in their own manufacturing operations.

issues.definition: When a scarce mineral lease is considered amid competing industrial needs, comparative captive requirements, equitable distribution, and effective exploitation are relevant considerations.

issues.legal_issue: A lease renewal decision based on a specialized committee’s technical and policy assessment may be upheld when the decision-maker adopts that assessment and the court does not substitute its own judgment on policy or technical matters.
material_facts: A high-level committee examined the competing claims and technical issues and recommended a reduced lease area based on the leaseholder’s requirements and the needs of other manufacturers.
The Central Government considered the committee’s analysis and authorized renewal over a reduced area, giving reasons for the reduction.
The dispute involved technical questions and policy choices concerning mineral development.
issues.conclusion: The Central Government was justified in issuing its renewal decision, and the appeals challenging that decision were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Act vests the Central Government with discretion over lease grants and renewals. Courts must exercise jurisdiction with circumspection where legal issues are intertwined with policy and technical questions, and should not enter the realm of policy-making unless the policy is inconsistent with the Constitution or the law. The Court deferred to the committee’s expertise on technical and policy matters.

predicates.lease_renewal_review_proceeding: A court reviewed a government decision on renewal of a mining lease.
predicates.expert_committee_made_technical_policy_a: A specialized committee assessed the technical and policy issues relevant to the lease decision.
predicates.government_order_followed_assessment: The government decision adopted the committee’s assessment in deciding the lease renewal.

issues.definition: In a lease renewal review, a government decision following a specialized committee’s technical and policy assessment is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A complaint that a committee failed to hear a claimant does not survive when the claimant is heard fully during the appeal.
material_facts: A claimant argued that the committee should have heard its claim when it heard the other parties.
The Supreme Court heard the claimant’s submissions at length.
issues.conclusion: The claimant’s grievance about not being heard by the committee did not survive, and its appeals failed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the opportunity to present the claimant’s case fully before it as removing the asserted grievance about the committee hearing. No earlier case or statutory provision was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.appeal_proceeding: A claimant appealed a decision made after a committee considered a lease matter.
predicates.claimant_was_not_heard_by_committee: The claimant asserted that the committee did not hear its claim.
predicates.claimant_heard_fully_on_appeal: The appellate court heard the claimant’s submissions at length.

issues.definition: In an appeal, a complaint about not being heard by a committee does not survive when the claimant is heard fully on appeal.
